result.topic_en: This spread (pp. 180–181) states corollaries of the interpolation example: trigonometric series for π cos mπ / sin mπ and related sums, and a product relation between Beta-type integrals ∫x^{n-1}dx(1−x)^{m-1}, whose proof is begun in a Scholion.
result.transcription:
[p. 180]
quae redigitur porro ad hanc:
$\int x^n dx(1-x)^{m-1} = \frac{(1-m)\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi}\cdot\frac{\int x^n dx(1-x)^{-2m}}{\int x^n dx(1-x)^{-m}},$
vel ad hanc adhuc concinniorem:
$\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{m-1} = \frac{2\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi}\cdot\frac{\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{-2m}}{\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{-m}}.$
Corollarium 1.
§. 26. En ergo aliquot insignia Theoremata, quae huius exempli euolutio nobis suppeditat, quorum primum est: Si $\phi$ denotet angulum quemcunque, erit
$\frac{\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi} = \frac{\cos. m\phi}{m} - \frac{\cos.(1-m)\phi}{1-m} + \frac{\cos.(1+m)\phi}{1+m} - \frac{\cos.(2-m)\phi}{2-m} + \text{etc.}$
quae aequalitas etiam ita exhiberi potest, vt sit:
$\frac{\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi} = \cos. m\phi\left(\frac{1}{m} - \frac{2m\cos.\phi}{1-mm} - \frac{2m\cos.2\phi}{4-mm} - \frac{2m\cos.3\phi}{9-mm} - \text{etc.}\right)$
$- 2\sin. m\phi\left(\frac{\sin.\phi}{1-mm} + \frac{2\sin.2\phi}{4-mm} + \frac{3\sin.3\phi}{9-mm} + \frac{4\sin.4\phi}{16-mm} - \text{etc.}\right)$
vnde si $m\phi = 90^\circ = \frac{\pi}{2}$, ideoque $\phi = \frac{\pi}{2m}$, erit
$\frac{\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi} = \frac{\sin.\frac{\pi}{2m}}{1-mm} + \frac{2\sin.\frac{2\pi}{2m}}{4-mm} + \frac{3\sin.\frac{3\pi}{2m}}{9-mm} + \frac{4\sin.\frac{4\pi}{2m}}{16-mm} + \text{etc.}$
Corollarium 2.
§. 27. Secundum Theorema ita enunciatur: Si $\phi$ denotet angulum quemcunque, erit:
$\frac{\pi\phi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi} = \frac{\sin. m\phi}{mm} - \frac{\sin.(1-m)\phi}{(1-m)^2} + \frac{\sin.(1+m)\phi}{(1+m)^2} - \frac{\sin.(2-m)\phi}{(2-m)^2} + \text{etc.}$
Quare sumto $\phi = \pi$ erit
$\frac{\pi\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi} = \frac{\sin. m\pi}{mm} - \frac{\sin. m\pi}{(1-m)^2} - \frac{\sin. m\pi}{(1+m)^2} + \frac{\sin. m\pi}{(2-m)^2} + \frac{\sin. m\pi}{(2+m)^2} - \text{etc.}$
siue
[p. 181]
siue
$\frac{\pi\pi}{\sin. m\pi\,\tang. m\pi} = \frac{1}{mm} - \frac{1}{(1-m)^2} - \frac{1}{(1+m)^2} + \frac{1}{(2-m)^2} + \frac{1}{(2+m)^2} - \text{etc.}$
At posito $m\phi = \pi$ habebitur
$\frac{\pi\pi\cos. m\pi}{m\sin. m\pi} = \frac{\sin.\frac{\pi}{m}}{(1-m)^2} - \frac{\sin.\frac{\pi}{m}}{(1+m)^2} + \frac{\sin.\frac{2\pi}{m}}{(2-m)^2} - \frac{\sin.\frac{2\pi}{m}}{(2+m)^2} + \text{etc.}$
siue hoc modo:
$\frac{\pi\pi\cos. m\pi}{4mm\sin. m\pi} = \frac{1\sin.\frac{\pi}{m}}{(1-mm)^2} + \frac{2\sin.\frac{2\pi}{m}}{(4-mm)^2} + \frac{3\sin.\frac{3\pi}{m}}{(9-mm)^2} + \text{etc.}$
Corollarium 3.
§. 28. Tertium Theorema spectat ad comparationem formularum integralium, et ita enunciatur: Si sequentium formularum integratio a termino $x = 0$ vsque ad terminum $x = 1$ extendatur, erit semper:
$\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{m-1}\cdot\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{-m}$
$= \frac{2\pi\cos. m\pi}{\sin. m\pi}\int x^{n-1}dx(1-x)^{-2m}.$
Seu si ponatur $m = \frac{\lambda}{n}$ et $x = y^n$, erit
$\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{n-\lambda}}}\cdot\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{\lambda}}} = \frac{2\pi\cos.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}{n\sin.\frac{\lambda\pi}{n}}\int\frac{y^{\lambda-1}dy}{\sqrt[n]{(1-y^n)^{2\lambda}}}.$
Scholion.
§. 29. Demonstratio huius postremi Theorematis non parum ardua videtur: interim tamen per ea, quae olim de huiusmodi formulis integralibus sum commentatus, eius veritas sequenti modo ostendi potest. Indicemus enim, vti ibi feci, hanc formulam integralem:
Z 3

items.english: If φ denotes any angle whatever, then π cos mπ / sin mπ = cos mφ/m − cos(1−m)φ/(1−m) + cos(1+m)φ/(1+m) − cos(2−m)φ/(2−m) + etc.

items.english: If φ denotes any angle whatever, then πφ cos mπ / sin mπ = sin mφ/m² − sin(1−m)φ/(1−m)² + sin(1+m)φ/(1+m)² − sin(2−m)φ/(2−m)² + etc.

items.quote: Si sequentium formularum integratio a termino $x = 0$ vsque ad terminum $x = 1$ extendatur, erit semper:
items.english: If the integration of the following formulas is extended from x = 0 to x = 1, then it will always hold that ∫x^{n−1}dx(1−x)^{m−1} · ∫x^{n−1}dx(1−x)^{−m} = (2π cos mπ / sin mπ) ∫x^{n−1}dx(1−x)^{−2m}.

items.quote: Demonstratio huius postremi Theorematis non parum ardua videtur: interim tamen per ea, quae olim de huiusmodi formulis integralibus sum commentatus, eius veritas sequenti modo ostendi potest.
